lead.headline: Nvidia halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
lead.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. The halt follows tighter US export controls meant to stop Chinese companies from renting computing power from foreign cloud providers. Cloud providers in the region have 90 days to apply for a license, and it is unclear whether the pause is temporary. CNBC reported that dealers have listed an unusually large number of Nvidia GPUs for sale, including thousands of B300 chips, and the FT reported that banks halted about $500 million in loans to Singapore-based provider Aolani.

main.headline: OpenAI corrects GPT-6.2 billing error, cutting usage limits
main.summary: OpenAI says a billing bug at the GPT-6.2 launch gave most users the wrong discounts on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. After the fix, users hit limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week, according to OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux. OpenAI will not charge users retroactively. Go, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers get an extra usage reset, and Business users get free Fast Mode through the end of the year.

main.headline: Report links US Nvidia partners to Chinese owners and export cases
main.summary: A C4ADS investigation requested by CBS News found that RiCloud AI, a San Jose-based Nvidia preferred partner, is a unit of Shenzhen-based Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings. It also linked Topmost Corp. to a California businessman recently indicted for allegedly smuggling GPUs to China. California-based Aivres, a subsidiary of Inspur, which is on the US Entity List, has exported $3 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to Southeast Asia since 2024, the report said.

main.headline: FCC approves SpaceX plan for up to 1 million orbital data center satellites
main.summary: The Federal Communications Commission authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites to process AI data in orbit, the BBC and Reuters report. Deployment must begin by November 2033, with 10% deployed by November 2035 and 50% by November 2038. Amazon called the plan a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan," and the American Astronomical Society said it would undermine the study of the night sky. SpaceX says it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year.

main.headline: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs, Bloomberg reports
main.summary: SAP is preparing to cut at least 10,000 positions, or more than 9% of its workforce, Bloomberg reported, citing sources. The scope may change. Product, engineering and sales units are expected to see the largest cuts, and a reported agreement with a German labor council guarantees employment there through 2028. SAP said it "continuously reviews its organization" to stay aligned with strategy and customer needs.

main.headline: Microsoft says state-backed hackers use ARTEX AI attack framework
main.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence says hacking groups from China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon and Onyx Sleet, have added the ARTEX framework to their operations, as have financially motivated criminals. ARTEX uses AI agents to run existing tools such as Metasploit and can connect to almost any large language model. Microsoft says it can move from reconnaissance to privileged access in minutes. Microsoft recommends honeypots, tarpits and "fake wins" that make the agent stop on its own, along with rate limits and phishing-resistant sign-in.
